title: Crew-12 Astronauts Splash Down in the Pacific After Nearly Eight Months in Space
summary: The four members of NASA's SpaceX Crew-12 mission returned to Earth on Oct. 8, 2026, after nearly eight months aboard the International Space Station. A NASA photograph shows their spacecraft moments before it touched down in the ocean.

sections.heading: Splashdown Off California
sections.body: SpaceX's Crew Dragon Freedom spacecraft landed in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of California on Oct. 8, 2026. This kind of return is called a splashdown because the capsule comes down in water rather than on land. A photograph taken by NASA's Keegan Barber captures the spacecraft just moments before it hit the water.

sections.heading: Four Crew Members Aboard
sections.body: Crew-12 carried four people home. NASA astronauts Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway were joined by Sophie Adenot, an astronaut with ESA (the European Space Agency), and Andrey Fedyaev, a cosmonaut with Roscosmos. Cosmonaut is the title used for Roscosmos's space travelers. The crew represented three different space organizations.

sections.heading: Months on the Space Station
sections.body: The four spent nearly eight months aboard the International Space Station, the orbiting laboratory where crews live and work in space. Their return brings the Crew-12 mission to a close. NASA has also published more photos from the splashdown for anyone who wants a closer look.
